title: Stop using a mixed grip
summary: Rant against the mixed (over/under) deadlift grip for anyone but competing powerlifters who can't hook grip. It risks biceps tears, creates rotation, trap and lower back asymmetries that spill into other lifts, and distracts from deadlift form. Use double overhand with straps (or hook grip) instead.

claims.claim: Lifting should be driven by your goals, not by the rules of the most numerous community on YouTube fitness (powerlifting).
The mixed grip (one hand pronated, one supinated) stops the bar rolling out of the hands and lets you deadlift more weight.

Mixed grip is dangerous for the biceps because the supinated arm puts the biceps tendon in a compromising position; he has never seen a biceps tear with double overhand, and strongmen pulling with straps don't tear biceps.
Keeping the arms straight makes mixed grip less dangerous than bending them, but still dangerous.

Mixed grip effectively makes one arm longer, creating bar rotation (helicopter deadlifts), uneven trap and upper back stimulation, and torsion that stresses one area of the lower back, leading to overuse injury.
Only powerlifters who must compete under grip rules and cannot hook grip should use mixed grip.
He used mixed grip for every pull two years earlier when training for powerlifting without ever competing, and now regrets it.
Doing all deadlift variations with mixed grip compounds the imbalance.
He has scoliosis with one shoulder lower, so mixed grip happened not to worsen his symmetry; people without it create an imbalance.
He has heard of lifters whose mixed grip grew one trap more, leading to crooked benching and shoulder injury.
Mixed grip makes you focus on the grip instead of the deadlift, which can lead to rounded backs and less than full effort.
The solution is straps, especially for bodybuilders; there's no point risking a biceps tear to prove you can hold the bar.
Powerlifters should give hook grip a real try despite small hands or pain, and only use mixed grip after exhausting alternatives.
Non-competitors should pull double overhand and use straps (or hook grip if they like it); beginners should not use mixed grip at all, at least through their first deadlift progression to 300 lbs.
Using mixed grip on shrugs or rows is not OK, and using straps with a mixed grip makes no sense for non-powerlifters.
